{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The ferry stopped running the winter Ilse turned nine, and her mother, who had sold tickets from the little booth on the pier for nineteen years, was given two weeks' notice and a box of unsold timetables. The box sat in the pantry. Her mother used the timetables to light the stove.

Ilse still walked down to the pier each morning before school. No one told her to. A bridge had opened upriver, wide and gray and humming with trucks, and the ferry itself had been towed to a yard on the coast where boats went to be cut apart. But her mother had taught her to read the river before the bridge was finished, how the color changed over the sandbar and how the eddies gathered leaves where the bottom dropped away, and the knowledge stayed even after the reason for it had gone.

From the end of the pier she could see the current bend around the old pilings, the water bright and quick where the channel ran, dark and sluggish near the bank.

One morning in late November a man in waders stood chest-deep beside the pilings, casting for pike, drifting a step at a time toward the place where the bottom fell off.

Ilse did not call out. She picked up a flat stone and skipped it three times across the calm water to his left, the way her mother had once signaled the deckhands.

He looked up. She pointed to the bank. He stepped back, felt the shelf under his boot, and understood.

"Who taught you that?" he asked when he had climbed out.

Ilse thought of the timetables curling in the stove and said, "Someone who used to work here.""}
